questions.q: What counts as an exempting `==` pin in a top-level requirement?
choices: Only exact `==X.Y.Z` with no wildcard
Also `===` arbitrary equality
Also `==X.*` wildcard specifiers
Any specifier set that contains `==`, even combined with others like `!=`
doesn't matter

questions.q: Which sources count as a top-level requirements file?
choices: Only files passed with `-r` or as bootstrap positional requirements
Also requirements given directly on the command line
Also requirements from `--constraints` files
Only requirements files, not CLI arguments
doesn't matter

questions.q: If a package has a top-level `==` pin and is also pulled in as a transitive dependency by another package, what happens?
choices: Exempt everywhere, since the pin applies to the package
Exempt only for the top-level resolution; transitive resolution still enforces the cooldown
Exempt only if the transitive specifier is also compatible with the pin
doesn't matter

questions.q: How should the exemption be reported?
choices: Log an info message that the cooldown is bypassed for the pinned package
Debug log only
No logging
doesn't matter

questions.q: How does the exemption interact with the per-package `resolver_dist.min_release_age` setting and the global `--min-release-age` option?
choices: The `==` pin bypasses both the global and per-package values
The `==` pin bypasses only the global value; an explicit per-package value still applies
The per-package value overrides the pin in either direction
doesn't matter
